intro.title: Welcome to Automation
intro.text: The Wireless Terminal lets you see and control your linked devices. Blue watches a machine. Yellow sends redstone. Green shows its contents. You can use SIMPLE buttons or write CODE.

intro.title: Link your devices
intro.text: Carry your own Wireless Terminal. Normally right-click a machine face with Blue and a receiving machine face with Yellow. Each torch needs an empty adjacent block. Existing torches can be linked by right-clicking them with your terminal.

intro.title: Name your controls
intro.text: Open Controls and rename the Yellow Stick to Pump, or another clear name. Code uses that exact name inside quotes. Names are case-sensitive. Two controls with the same name are an error, not a random choice.

intro.title: Open Code Mode
intro.text: Open the terminal, choose Automation, select a Blue device, then CODE. Type your program, click Save, then Enable. SIMPLE rules stay saved. Only the selected mode runs.

intro.title: Your first program
intro.text: Put Blue on a chest and name a Yellow control Pump. Save this program. Adding stone makes Pump send five seconds of redstone.

intro.title: WHEN, THEN, END
intro.text: WHEN checks something. THEN chooses an action. END finishes one rule. Put each on its own line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are allowed. Keywords can use upper or lower case.

intro.title: Reading amounts
intro.text: >= means greater than or equal to: at least that amount. < means less than. Amounts are whole numbers from 0 through 1000000000000. Item IDs look like minecraft:stone.

intro.title: Understanding mB
intro.text: mb means millibuckets. One normal bucket is 1000 mB. 200mb is one fifth of a bucket. Fluid data comes from real exposed tanks; the script never estimates a fill level.

intro.title: Which fluid name?
intro.text: Hover a tank in Monitors to see its Fluid ID. Forge water is water. HBM IDs are shown as hbm: followed by its actual registry name. A common unqualified name also matches the same HBM name. Display names are not IDs.

intro.title: A rule fires once
intro.text: Without EVERY, a rule fires once when false becomes true. Stable true does not repeat. Drop below the threshold and reach it again for another pulse. Add EVERY before THEN to repeat while true.

intro.title: Repeat while true
intro.text: EVERY is optional. Put it between WHEN and THEN. The first true check triggers immediately; later true checks trigger once per interval. False stops and resets the timer. s means seconds, m minutes, h hours. Use whole positive amounts. Time uses server ticks at 20 TPS; stopped servers do not advance timers.
intro.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" >= 200mb
EVERY 20s
THEN PULSE "WATER" 5s
END

intro.title: More than one rule
intro.text: Put up to eight WHEN/THEN/END blocks in one editor. Each keeps its own true/false memory and optional repeat timer. When several actions are due for one target in the same poll, the last block in text order wins.

intro.title: Pulses and manual power
intro.text: PULSE lasts 5-10 seconds. ON stays on; OFF stops immediately. ON/OFF cancel a running timer. A pulse already running ignores another pulse. Across separate Blue devices, server processing order decides the latest accepted command.

intro.title: Saving and switching
intro.text: An invalid Save keeps the draft and last working program. Save does not enable disabled code. Switching SIMPLE/CODE keeps both programs. Unchanged rules retain their edge and EVERY deadline. Disable stops checks; active pulses finish, and manual ON stays on until OFF.

intro.title: Unloaded machines
intro.text: Devices must be loaded in the same dimension. Scripts do not load chunks. Missing data never becomes zero. Affected rules keep their edge and repeat deadline. On return, an overdue true EVERY runs once and schedules from now, without a catch-up burst.

intro.title: What this cannot do
intro.text: Commands only read supported storage and control your linked Yellow Sticks. They cannot transfer items, create RF/HE, run Java, or control a machine that ignores vanilla redstone. Other HBM forks and unverified multiblocks may show FLUID DATA UNAVAILABLE.

conditions.syntax:
WHEN ITEM "item_id" >= amount
WHEN ITEM "item_id" < amount
conditions.text: Count a real item. >= means at least; < means fewer than.
conditions.limits: Use registered item IDs. CODE counts all metadata/NBT variants of that item; use SIMPLE ghost rules for exact variants.

conditions.text: Check whether all accessible inventory slots are empty.
conditions.example:
WHEN INVENTORY EMPTY
THEN PULSE "Pump" 5s
END
conditions.limits: A missing or unsupported inventory is unavailable, not empty.

conditions.text: Check whether accessible slots have no known spare stack space.
conditions.example:
WHEN INVENTORY FULL
THEN PULSE "Pump" 5s
END
conditions.result: A full chest triggers a storage warning once.
conditions.limits: Empty opaque slots count as available. Hidden custom slot limits cannot be inferred. SIMPLE can test fullness for one ghost item.

conditions.syntax:
WHEN FLUID "fluid_id" >= amountmb
WHEN FLUID "fluid_id" < amountmb
conditions.text: Count actual millibuckets of the named fluid across the exposed tanks.
conditions.result: 100 mB is false. Reaching 200 mB triggers seven seconds of redstone.
conditions.limits: Matching amounts are summed across the selected Forge face. HBM uses its public supported tank set; fluid-enabled proxies resolve the loaded controller. Hover a Green monitor tank to copy its ID. Unknown names are rejected; unavailable reads pause the rule.

conditions.text: Check whether every exposed supported tank contains no liquid.
conditions.example:
WHEN TANK EMPTY
THEN PULSE "Pump" 5s
END
conditions.result: The empty tank set triggers once.
conditions.limits: All exposed tanks are considered, not only water. No supported tanks means unavailable.

conditions.text: Check whether every exposed positive-capacity tank has reached capacity.
conditions.example:
WHEN TANK FULL
THEN PULSE "Pump" 5s
END
conditions.result: A full tank set triggers once.
conditions.limits: Every exposed tank must be full. Zero-capacity tanks do not count; a set with no positive capacity is unavailable.

actions.syntax:
THEN PULSE "Control Name" 5s
THEN PULSE "Control Name"
actions.text: Send redstone power 15 for five through ten seconds, then return to zero.
actions.result: Pump turns on for 140 server ticks at 20 TPS.
actions.limits: Without a duration, use the Yellow Stick's configured duration. An already active timed pulse ignores another pulse and keeps its original deadline. This command works even if the target is configured Manual.

actions.text: Set redstone output to 15 until an OFF command or a later pulse changes it.
actions.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:iron_ingot" >= 64
THEN ON "Machine Power"
END
actions.limits: ON cancels an existing pulse timer. It does not change the target's saved mode/duration settings.

actions.text: Set redstone output to zero now.
actions.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:coal" < 16
THEN OFF "Machine Power"
END
actions.result: Machine Power turns off and its pulse timer is canceled.
actions.limits: The receiving machine must accept vanilla redstone on that face.

examples.title: Stone starter
examples.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:stone" >= 1
THEN PULSE "Stone Processor" 5s
END
examples.text: Add stone to the attached chest. Stone Processor pulses once.

examples.title: Stack of iron
examples.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:iron_ingot" >= 64
THEN PULSE "Factory Machine" 10s
END
examples.text: Store at least 64 iron ingots. Factory Machine pulses for ten seconds.

examples.title: Low coal warning
examples.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:coal" < 16
THEN PULSE "Coal Warning" 7s
END
examples.text: Fewer than 16 coal triggers the warning. Refill before another low edge.

examples.title: Empty chest
examples.example:
WHEN INVENTORY EMPTY
THEN PULSE "Refill System" 5s
END
examples.text: Remove the last item from the chest to trigger Refill System.

examples.title: Full chest
examples.example:
WHEN INVENTORY FULL
THEN PULSE "Storage Alarm" 5s
END
examples.text: Fill all accessible slots to trigger Storage Alarm.

examples.title: Water at 200 mB
examples.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" >= 200mb
THEN PULSE "Arc Furnace" 7s
END
examples.text: Start below 200 mB, then add water. Arc Furnace pulses once for seven seconds.

examples.title: Oil at 1000 mB
examples.example:
WHEN FLUID "oil" >= 1000mb
THEN PULSE "Oil Pump" 5s
END
examples.text: Needs an installed fluid registered as oil. Hover its tank for the actual ID if different.

examples.title: Empty tank
examples.example:
WHEN TANK EMPTY
THEN PULSE "Empty Tank Alarm" 5s
END
examples.text: An exposed empty tank set triggers the alarm.

examples.title: Turn power on
examples.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:stone" >= 64
THEN ON "Machine Power"
END

examples.title: Turn power off
examples.example:
WHEN ITEM "minecraft:stone" < 16
THEN OFF "Machine Power"
END

examples.title: Refill water
examples.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" < 500mb
THEN PULSE "Water Refill" 10s
END
examples.text: Low water starts Water Refill for ten seconds.

examples.title: Full tank alarm
examples.example:
WHEN TANK FULL
THEN PULSE "Tank Full Alarm" 5s
END
examples.text: All exposed tanks reaching capacity starts the alarm.

examples.title: Repeat water every 20 seconds
examples.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" >= 200mb
EVERY 20s
THEN PULSE "WATER" 5s
END
examples.text: Name your Yellow Stick WATER. At 200 mB or more, trigger immediately and every twenty seconds while true. Below 200 mB stops repeats.

examples.title: Repeat water every 20 minutes
examples.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" >= 200mb
EVERY 20m
THEN PULSE "WATER" 5s
END
examples.text: Name your Yellow Stick WATER. At 200 mB or more, trigger immediately and every twenty minutes while true. Below 200 mB stops repeats.

examples.title: Repeat water every 20 hours
examples.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" >= 200mb
EVERY 20h
THEN PULSE "WATER" 5s
END
examples.text: Name your Yellow Stick WATER. At 200 mB or more, trigger immediately and every twenty hours while true. Below 200 mB stops repeats.

troubleshooting.title: Unknown item
troubleshooting.text: Check the full registered ID, such as minecraft:iron_ingot. CODE item checks count all variants of that item. If removing a mod makes a saved ID unknown, the program disables until you fix and save it.

troubleshooting.title: Unknown fluid
troubleshooting.text: Copy the Fluid ID shown when hovering a tank in Monitors. A fluid that is not installed cannot be used. Unknown fluid is a Save error, not zero mB. If removing a mod makes a saved ID unknown, the program disables until you fix and save it.

troubleshooting.title: Unknown control
troubleshooting.text: Rename a Yellow Stick in Controls, then use its exact name inside quotes. If names are duplicated, rename one or use "id:UUID" from the control tooltip. Controls must belong to this terminal and dimension.

troubleshooting.title: Invalid command
troubleshooting.text: Use only documented WHEN conditions and THEN PULSE/ON/OFF actions. Check quotes, whole numbers, mb, and s. The error tells you which line to fix.

troubleshooting.title: Missing END
troubleshooting.text: Add END on its own line after each THEN action.

troubleshooting.title: Target offline
troubleshooting.text: Load the machine and Yellow Stick chunks with your existing chunk loader if needed. Scripts wait and never force-load them.

troubleshooting.title: Unsupported machine
troubleshooting.text: Mount Blue directly on a readable inventory or tank face. Plain ground has no storage. Unknown APIs report unavailable instead of triggering low-resource rules.

troubleshooting.title: No permission
troubleshooting.text: Use your own bound terminal and linked sticks. A stolen terminal or a control from another network is rejected.

troubleshooting.title: Repeat not firing
troubleshooting.text: Place EVERY 20s, 20m or 20h on its own line between WHEN and THEN. Save and enable CODE. Keep the tank and Yellow control loaded. Each active pulse ignores another pulse; use a longer interval than pulse duration for an OFF gap. Server shutdown time does not count.

glossary.text: Seconds: 5s is five seconds at 20 TPS.
Repeat while true after the chosen interval.
Minutes: 20m is twenty minutes at 20 TPS.
Hours: 20h is twenty hours at 20 TPS.

timing.syntax:
WHEN condition
EVERY 20s
THEN action
END
timing.text: Repeat the action while the condition stays true. Use EVERY 5s, 10s, 20s, 20m or 20h. The first true check runs immediately, then the interval is measured from each due action. Use one EVERY line between WHEN and THEN.
timing.example:
WHEN FLUID "water" >= 200mb
EVERY 20s
THEN PULSE "WATER" 5s
END
timing.result: WATER pulses for five seconds immediately at 200 mB or more, then again every twenty seconds while water stays at least 200 mB.
timing.limits: Whole positive s/m/h durations only, with overflow rejected. Pulse length remains 5-10s. An active pulse ignores another pulse, so choose an interval longer than the pulse to get a visible OFF gap. False resets the timer. Unavailable data/targets pause actions. Timers and unchanged saves survive restarts; overdue rules run once on resume, never a burst. Timings use server ticks, so lag may delay them.
